old: Like one who, on a lonely road, Doth walk in fear and dread, And, having once turned round, walks on, And turns no more his head; Because he knows a frightful fiend Doth close behind him tread.
new: Like one who, on a lonely road, walks on in fear and dread, and, having once turned round, walks on and turns his head no more, because he knows a frightful fiend is treading close behind him.
reason: Protocol: modernize quoted verse (Coleridge, Ancient Mariner). Archaic 'Doth' forms replaced; every image kept (lonely road, fear and dread, turned round once, frightful fiend close behind); rhyme yields to meaning.

old: Man's yesterday may ne'er be like his morrow; Nought may endure but mutability!
new: Man's yesterday may never be like his morrow; nothing may endure but mutability — change itself!
reason: Protocol: modernize quoted verse (Percy Shelley, 'Mutability'). ne'er/Nought modernized; the title word 'mutability' kept with a brief gloss for listeners.
